answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a bond in a scarce resource, then slash it if the identity is caught duplicating votes or breaking task rules. A reputation-weighted committee checks evidence before slashing, and newcomers gain influence gradually through completed work. A sybil attacker must lock up real capital for every name, risking its loss; splitting one budget cannot multiply voting power. The same rule can protect an oasis project, a comet survey, or a yarrow harvest.
